requiredFindings.title: Review-list equality accepts a different JSON selector
requiredFindings.law: VD2 r1 rule 2.7; canonical selector identity in rule 2.3
requiredFindings.description: Python equality treats true as 1 and 1.0 as 1. A valid contract supersession selecting line 1 verifies even when its independently pinned review lists selector {"line": true} or {"line": 1.0}. Those are different canonical selectors and neither is a valid integer line selector. The record still selects the right passage, but the explicit review does not list that passage exactly.
requiredFindings.reproduction: Run value-equality-probes.py with the recorded private environment: its first two cases currently PASSED with contractPassageSupersessions 1; they must refuse with contract review superseded passages differ from the record.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Make the new review-list comparison respect JSON types and canonical selector identity, while preserving list order, object-key-order independence, the existing refusal message and VD1 target-pin behavior. Add negative regression cases for a boolean and floating-point review line selector against an integer selector in the record.
requiredFindings.f8cConsequence: Correcting the verifier changes the reference candidate, tool-only diff, closure and lane pins, registry digest, generated report headers, evidence and subject/record pins. Refresh F8c on the corrected bytes and rerun the requested checks before seeking acceptance of the coupled unit.

vd2Nb01Disposition.evidence: All six controls are present in ContractPassageSupersessionTests and all 46 extension controls pass. The rewritten VD1 positive half supplies the list and asserts count 1, inventory count 0 and the named supersedes; its inventory-negative half remains.

judgmentCalls.answer: Agree with v4-only scope and the numbered per-record checking order. Earlier lock versions remain unchanged, and conflicting overrides retain their original refusal precedence.

Keep VD1-compatible target-pin equality: an exact path and digest with numerically equal byte length cannot name different content, and named selectors remain canonical. Require a type-aware comparison for the newly added review list: its boolean or floating-point selector currently bypasses explicit exact review coverage. See VD2A-RF-01.

Keep the root-kind guard as a stated invariant. A published contract supersession already set that passage tail; the one mutation survivor is therefore unreachable, not an uncovered reachable refusal.
The optional listed argument preserves legacy fixtures; AUTO supplies exact lists for new controls. N15 correctly exercises the unchanged v3 refusal before classification.
The three I1-a and two F8b parents match the five accepted base pins at 4c761e8. No closure-writer substitution or serialization drift was found.

Keep the tool-only diff. It equals the product tool diff and applies to the F8b parent to produce the candidate exactly. It provides non-circular provenance; carrying the full lock-containing unit diff would be circular.
Use a unit review and a separate contract review. The latter has the contract verdict and is the file eligible for binding after acceptance; neither review grants acceptance in this round.
No inventory successor is required. No path is added, all seven changed paths are rows of v135, and their descriptions remain true. Neither JSON review includes inventoryCandidateAssessment.

The bounded Rust lanes are appropriate. No Rust source reads the changed tool/re-pin files. Independently reran fmt, both metadata lanes, package/dependency checks and the optional 25-test schema_sources suite.
